In deep RL, the **"treacherous turn"** has been reproduced with trojan-injection training, though it did not emerge naturally from environmental complexity alone (\cite[Ashcraft et al., 2025]{treacherous_turn}).

blocks.quote: Long before deep learning, Norbert Wiener warned that a machine built to pursue a fixed goal would not share our sense of when to stop: we had better be sure the purpose we put in is the purpose we want (\cite[Wiener, 1960]{wiener1960moral}). Isaac Asimov's Three Laws (1942) were a fictional attempt to encode safety as rules, and *Runaround* already stages their failure—conflicting instructions produce a literal-minded, dangerous deadlock (\cite[Asimov, 1942]{asimov1942runaround}). In 1965 I. J. Good described an "intelligence explosion" and called the first ultraintelligent machine "the last invention that man need ever make" (\cite[Good, 1965]{good1965explosion}).
blocks.section: Empirical evidence that it is real, not hypothetical

blocks.quote: The research agenda acquired institutions. The Asilomar AI Principles (2017) gathered researchers around 23 principles—safety, failure transparency, value alignment, and long-term caution (\cite[Future of Life Institute, 2017]{asilomar2017}). The Bletchley Declaration (November 2023) put 28 countries and the EU behind frontier-AI safety cooperation (\cite[UK Government, 2023]{bletchley2023}); the EU AI Act (2024) turned similar principles into binding duties (\cite[EU, 2024]{euaiact2024}). Britain's AI Safety Institute (2023, now the AI Security Institute) and a network of national counterparts were built to evaluate frontier models and share testing practice (\cite[UK AISI, 2023]{aisi2023}).
blocks.section: Empirical evidence that it is real, not hypothetical

blocks.quote: Soft law supplies the vocabulary that hard law borrows. The OECD AI Principles (2019, revised 2024) define human-centred values, transparency, robustness, and accountability (\cite[OECD, 2019]{oecd2019ai}); UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI (2021) was adopted by all 193 member states and adds proportionality, sustainability, and oversight (\cite[UNESCO, 2021]{unesco2021ai}). In the United States the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (2023) became the de facto vocabulary for "govern, map, measure, manage" (\cite[NIST, 2023]{nist2023airmf}). The 2023 Biden executive order on safe AI was revoked in January 2025, leaving standards and state law to fill the gap (\cite[White House, 2023]{eo14110}).

blocks.quote: The methods
The current toolkit

The modern toolkit is a menu, not a fixed pipeline: **SFT** (demonstrations), then either **RLHF** (a learned reward model from human preferences, introduced by **Paul Christiano** and colleagues in 2017), **RLAIF / Constitutional AI** (AI feedback instead), or **direct preference optimization** (DPO and successors), which learns the policy directly without an explicit RL loop. (\cite[Christiano et al., 2017]{christiano2017rlhf}; \cite[Ouyang et al., 2022]{ouyang2022instructgpt}; \cite[Lee et al., 2023]{rlaif}; \cite[Bai et al., 2022]{bai2022constitutional})
The models also acquire **self-knowledge**: they track their own accuracy surprisingly well, which is a cheap, usable reliability lever. (\cite[Kadavath et al., 2022]{kadavath2022selfknowledge})
The two big research programs
Interpretability as a safety tool

You cannot supervise what you cannot see. **Mechanistic interpretability** — sparse autoencoders, circuit discovery, activation steering — is increasingly applied as a *safety* instrument: to find the "safety circuit" (detection heads $\to$ safety neurons $\to$ refusal heads), to spot a backdoor's signature in later layers, and to build **abstention** — letting the model say *I don't know* rather than bluff. (\cite[Naseem, 2026]{mech_interp_alignment})

The line now runs both ways. A model that can locate a behaviour's direction in the weights can remove it as well as repair it, so an LLM that edits weights is both an auditing instrument and a way to strip a safety behaviour without data (\cite[Takehi et al., 2026]{takehi2026weightspace}).
